title: Spinoza was expelled from his community at 23 and lived by grinding lenses

cover.alt: A bronze statue of Baruch Spinoza in a long coat, on a stone base beside a canal at Zwanenburgwal in Amsterdam.

body: On 27 July 1656 the leaders of Amsterdam’s Portuguese-Jewish community issued a herem, a writ of expulsion, against the 23-year-old Baruch Spinoza for ‘abominable heresies’ and ‘monstrous deeds’ it never specified. Cut off, he supported himself by grinding lenses and building microscopes and telescopes, work that Christiaan Huygens and other scientists praised. He turned down a professorship at Heidelberg, possibly to keep his freedom of thought. His great work, the Ethics, appeared only after his death in 1677, aged 44, from a lung disease, probably tuberculosis and possibly worsened by the glass dust of his trade.

events.text: Expelled from Amsterdam’s Jewish community by a herem, aged 23
Dies in The Hague; friends publish the Ethics

slides.question: In what year was the Ethics finally published?
slides.explanation: 1677, the year he died. His friends issued it in the Opera Posthuma with the publisher’s name and the place of printing deliberately left off.

steps.label: Huygens and others praise their quality
Glass dust may have harmed his lungs

slides.question: What did the 1656 writ say Spinoza had done?
slides.explanation: The herem spoke of ‘abominable heresies’ and ‘monstrous deeds’ but gave no specifics. The exact reason is not stated.

slides.heading: Published in secret
slides.text: His friends issued his works in 1677 as the Opera Posthuma, with the publisher and place of printing deliberately left off. The Ethics, finished around 1674, is built like Euclid’s geometry, from definitions and axioms to proofs, and argues that God is identical with the universe: Deus sive Natura, ‘God or Nature’.

slides.alt: The Spinoza statue by Nicolas Dings seen from the Zwanenburgwal canal in Amsterdam, with canal houses behind it.
slides.caption: Nicolas Dings’s 2008 statue stands at Zwanenburgwal in Amsterdam, near Spinoza’s birthplace.
